title: Mary Grace Baloyo, the Air Force's "Amazing Grace"
big_number_label: families were saved by her decision not to eject, according to her father
takeaways: On March 26, 2001, the engine of 1Lt. Mary Grace Baloyo's OV-10 Bronco failed as she was approaching Clark, Pampanga.
Her co-pilot ejected, but Grace stayed inside to steer the plane away from the houses in Mabalacat. It crashed into an empty lot.
She was the first woman in the Armed Forces of the Philippines to receive the Medal of Valor, the military's highest award.

quiz.q: What plane did Mary Grace Baloyo fly?
Where did her plane crash in 2001?
What award did she receive, as the first woman in the AFP?

paragraphs: Do you know who the first female soldier in the Philippines to receive the Medal of Valor was? It's the military's highest award for bravery. When her plane was going down, she had the chance to eject and survive. But she didn't. Her name was Mary Grace Baloyo. But to her fellow pilots, she was Amazing Grace. She grew up in Bacolod, the eldest of four siblings. When she said she wanted to be a pilot, her mother was against it at first. But eventually, she agreed. And in 1997, she graduated from the Philippine Air Force Flying School. And did you know? She wasn't just any pilot. She was one of the Air Force's six women combat pilots. The plane she flew: the OV-10 Bronco, an attack aircraft. She flew in the Mindanao campaign, at Camp Abubakar, and had already received several medals. She was only twenty-seven at the time, and was set to marry a fellow pilot the following year.

But on March 26, 2001, she flew from Cavite to Clark with her co-pilot, Captain Ben Nasayao. They were close to Clark when the engine suddenly failed. The plane was falling fast, toward a crowded area in Mabalacat, Pampanga. Seconds before the crash, Captain Nasayao ejected. He survived. But Grace? She did not eject. She stayed inside and forced the plane away from the houses. It crashed into an empty lot in the middle of a subdivision. Grace died instantly. According to her father, more than two hundred families were saved by that decision. As one resident put it: she died so we might live.

President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo awarded her the Medal of Valor and promoted her to Captain. And here's more! She was the first woman in the entire Armed Forces of the Philippines to receive it. As one newspaper put it at the time: she showed all of us how a soldier should die. Today, there is a statue of her in Bacolod, so that her heroism will never be forgotten.
